video.title: This One AI Prompt Could Land You a $15K Client

summary: Chris Koerner and Sam Thompson brainstorm business ideas enabled by ChatGPT's new image generation. They argue standalone novelty products (custom coloring books, print-on-demand art) are real but short-lived, and that the bigger opportunity is selling AI-generated personalised before/after mockups to home-service businesses (landscaping, painting, tree trimming, pool, remodel) for direct-mail and sales use. The pitch is a ~$500/month mockup tool or service sold to local contractors, found via Valpak mailers, plus tracked-number revenue-share deals. Key takeaway: the best marketer and channel wins, and the B2B application is less obvious than consumer novelty products. All numbers are speculative and untested.

ideas.name: AI before/after mockup service for landscaping and home-service companies
ideas.one_liner: Generate personalised AI mockups of prospects' own homes and sell the mockup tool or service, with direct mail, to local contractors.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription (~$500/month per contractor), or a percentage of jobs won via tracked phone number, or done-for-you mailers per postcard.
ideas.customer: Local landscaping, painting, pool, tree-trimming, remodel and home-builder companies, especially those already spending on direct mail.
ideas.problem: Homeowners cannot visualise the end result and are not designers, so friction stops them spending money; contractors' generic mailers have low response rates.
ideas.offer: Unlimited custom AI mockups, graphics and quotes for each prospect, integrated into the contractor's CRM or via a simple form (upload photo, budget, location, wants like pool or koi pond); or personalised postcards showing the prospect's own house.

pricing.model: Flat monthly subscription, or revenue share on jobs, or per-postcard

price_points.label: consumer-facing version of Sam's trip planner style tool

pricing.notes: Revenue share via tracked phone number as an alternative to fixed fee.

acquisition_channels.details: Find local businesses already buying direct mail via Valpak (valpac.com zip code lookup), then phone the owner, whose number is probably his cell, and show a mockup of his own yard.

quote.text: you can type in a zip code and see what ads they're running there and then you can find the local businesses that already find direct mail effective
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Text the owner a mockup of his own front yard, found using deep research for his address.
Personalised postcards with the prospect's house mockup, sent to homeowners to drive calls to the contractor.
Contractor sales reps generate a mockup live at the door in about five minutes.

ideas.delivery: AI image generation (ChatGPT/Sora) from Google Earth or Zillow photos produces mockups; direct-mail APIs and tools such as Banner Bear produce and send postcards; optional chat query to estimate job cost and home value uplift. Human sales closes the physical job.
unit_economics_claims: Direct mail conversion could rise from 0.5% to 5% with targeted mockups
Pool example: comps listed at 830k vs 700k
Garage conversion example: cost 24k, value 323k to 428k
ideas.startup_cost: Low; mainly image generation credits and postage (not stated precisely).
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Claimed testable same day with a mock mailer; not otherwise stated.

acquisition.how: Valpak lookup, deep research and mockup generation are scriptable, but cold calls/texts to sole-trader owners face UK PECR/TPS limits and still need human sales.

onboarding.how: A simple intake form (photo, budget, location) can be automated; CRM integration needs setup.

delivery.how: Image generation, mailer creation and cost estimates are largely agent-driven; accuracy checks needed and contractor does physical work.

support.how: Chat or email support is agent-handled; edge cases need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Concept works in the UK, but Valpak, Zillow and Google Earth workflows are US-centric; UK needs Rightmove/OS data, Royal Mail Door Drop and compliance with GDPR/PECR for addressed mail; cold texting owners is restricted.

risks: Image realism and accuracy of cost or value estimates could mislead customers
Fear-based fake damage mockups (fallen tree) are ethically and legally questionable
Contractor adoption is slow (host guesses ~10 years to reach 10% of landscapers)
GDPR/PECR and TPS rules in the UK
Everyone will copy once API is available

tactics.name: Find contractors already buying direct mail via Valpak
steps: Go to valpac.com and enter a zip code to see local advertisers
Shortlist businesses already spending on direct mail
Phone the owner and ask why they are wasting money on Valpak
Send a personalised mockup of the owner's own house or yard as proof
Offer to do it for all their customers, priced as a fee or a percentage of tracked jobs

quote.text: you can find the local businesses that already find direct mail effective. They're already spending on it. That's your lowest hanging fruit.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test the mailer before having a client
steps: Act as if you run a home remodeling company
Send AI mockup mailers to a target neighbourhood
Count the leads you get
Take the data to a real remodeler and offer to repeat it for them

tactics.name: Filter then personalise to raise direct-mail ROI
steps: Scrape house images for a city
Use AI to remove homes that do not fit (for example no trees in the front yard)
Generate improved versions for the remaining ones
Mail only the filtered set, for example about 100 of 10,000 homes

tactics.name: Put the maths on the picture
steps: Pull the home's current value from Zillow
Add estimated value after the project and the project cost
Print the profit on the mockup
Close with a clear call to action

tactics.name: Test niches with one general store
steps: Run one Shopify store with many products and test ads
Find the winning market (for example weddings)
Double down on it after testing about eight things

tactics.name: Brainstorm from Sora's most-liked feed
steps: Open Sora and sort by most liked
Read the prompt behind each design
Pick a simple wrapper idea based on one prompt

lessons.lesson: When a technology lowers the barrier to entry, the best marketer who finds the right channel, angle and price first wins.

quote.text: the marketer that finds the right channel angle pricing first
quote.speaker: Sam Thompson

lessons.lesson: Test price points: conversion rate times price decides which version earns more.
Selling B2B applications of new tools to existing businesses is likely more durable than novelty consumer products.
Remove customer friction by showing the end state; people don't know what they want or can afford until they see it.

quote.text: The friction between not knowing what it should look like will likely prevent them from ever spending that money
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Validate cheaply before approaching a client by running a small test campaign and bringing results to the business.
Use the business's real cost data (hourly rates, distances) with AI to get accurate quotes.
Target businesses already spending on a channel as the lowest-hanging fruit.
Prompting ChatGPT with memory about yourself for self-reflection can give language to define your strengths and weaknesses.

evidence_quality.rationale: Brainstorm-style conversation with hypothetical numbers and no tested results; the only first-hand figures concern a viral tweet. Ideas are plausible but unvalidated.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes his newsletter and podcast (tkopod.com) and runs a home-services business and agency; Sam builds AI tools and apps.
